title: Full stress stratifications determine a labelled graph
seo_title: Full stress stratifications and labelled graph reconstruction | Alec Kriebel
meta_description: An edge is detected by its collision diagonal in a graph's full connected sign-stress partition. A reconstruction theorem for fixed labelled graphs.
printed_date_and_status: 12 October 2026 (research note), no numeric version printed
abstract: For a simple labelled graph, consider the full configuration space, including vertex collisions, partitioned into connected components of coordinate-sign equivalence classes of self-stress spaces. We prove that two graphs induce identical partitions precisely when their edge sets agree. More explicitly, an edge is recovered by asking whether its collision diagonal is a union of strata. This answers the literal equality formulation of Karpenkov's Problem 4. The proof combines the known singleton-support collision criterion with an explicit positive diagonal transport along a collinear path. The comparison convention is essential: nonisomorphic trees can have ambient-linearly equivalent stratifications.

scientific_scope.corollary: A specified vertex permutation carries the partitions iff it carries the graphs
